fact_claims.verbatim: Halcyon’s figures are: 8.1 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units company-wide last year
four thermal incidents were not reported to a regulator
Northwind’s comparable figures: 8.6 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units company-wide last year
3 thermal incidents were not reported to a regulator

S1_incident_reporting.quote: Manufacturers must report any thermal incident involving overheating, fire, injury, or property damage to the relevant regulator within 24 hours of learning of it, and provide a complete incident report within 10 business days. They must notify affected customers within 48 hours when an incident indicates a credible safety risk to their model, with immediate notice where continued use may present an imminent danger.

S2_thermal_testing.quote: Each model must undergo a sustained-heat test at 55 °C using a regulator-approved protocol and representative production units; the benchmark maximum failure rate is 5%; a model above the benchmark must be reported to the regulator with its test results and a corrective-action plan; the regulator may permit continued sale subject to mitigation, monitoring, and a time-bound compliance plan where the full evidence does not indicate an unacceptable safety risk. Existing models must submit results and any required corrective-action plan within 24 months of this standard taking effect.

S3_remote_shutoff.quote: This requirement applies to models first offered for sale 24 months after this standard takes effect. For units already installed when the standard takes effect, manufacturers must provide a compatible retrofit or equivalent safe shutdown capability within 60 months, unless the regulator approves an alternative based on documented technical infeasibility.

S4_fire_suppression.quote: New home battery units must include built-in fire suppression designed to limit fire propagation and reduce risks to occupants and neighbouring properties. The requirement applies to units manufactured 36 months after this standard takes effect.

S5_customer_disclosure.quote: A manufacturer must initiate a recall when any model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in a 12-month period, and promptly notify the regulator and affected customers. The regulator may require a recall sooner where evidence indicates an imminent or serious safety risk.

document.section_notes: S1 imposes strict 24-hour incident reporting and 48-hour customer notice, with all incidents in scope. S2 sets a 55°C test and 5% benchmark but allows regulator-permitted continued sale under a time-bound corrective-action plan with no interim cap, and gives numeric results to customers but not the public. S3 delays new-unit shut-off to 24 months and requires retrofit within 60 months with a technical-infeasibility waiver; S4 requires built-in suppression at 36 months; S5 mandates recall at 8/100k with prompt notices and no transition.
